title: Shove · full displacement
description: A discovered STR18 shove wins its native contest and pushes the clothed recipient two cells. The original shove root owns its exact forced-movement and spatial descendants.

title: Shove · target resists
description: A real failed Athletics contest spends the bonus action without displacement. No forced-movement child or fake travel is created.

title: Shove · fully blocked
description: The real contest succeeds, but the next tile is occupied by another creature. Native zero-distance Shove has no forced-movement child.

title: Shove · partial displacement
description: The recipient crosses one tile, then an actual blocking creature stops the remaining intended distance. Retain native blocked status and final position.

title: Shove · leave an armed enemy
description: The target leaves the reach of a native armed Goblin carrying its normal opportunity handler. Forced movement emits spatial entries without voluntary Steps; the watcher keeps its reaction.

title: Shove · ascending stairs
description: A native allowed push ascends the published EARTH stair run from support height 0 to 2. Each spatial entry retains its actual support; compare the descending direction.

title: Shove · descending stairs
description: The reversed native push descends the published stair run from support height 2 to 0. Legal movement remains governed by the map transition rules.

title: Shove · packaged Goblin recipient

title: Shove → two spike entries
description: The real standard-arena spike field deals 5 then 7 damage as the recipient enters two cells. Both damage subtrees remain under their exact spatial entry, within one forced displacement.

title: Shove → lethal first spike entry
description: The recipient starts with native 4 HP. The first actual spike entry deals lethal damage and stops displacement at that reached cell; there is no later entry or invented landing.

title: Established Telekinesis · move recipient
description: The baseline follows a real successful Telekinesis cast and grab. Its discovered, zero-cost Move follow-up retains the complete native action/forced-movement/spatial lineage; no new casting media is authored here.

title: Opportunity attack → takeoff → land
description: The real second-Step opportunity subtree plays at the grounded launch contact. After the complete reaction, one uninterrupted body traversal spans the entire jump. Native Step commits and after-values remain authoritative.

title: Lethal opportunity attack → no takeoff
description: A real second-Step lethal reaction leaves the first native Step committed. The visual body stays grounded at launch through death and settlement; its legal endpoint remains the committed native position.

title: Short jump · forward
description: A discovered one-cell jump. The complete body clip spans its airtime and returns to Idle at landing; compare jump-clear for the reverse direction.

title: Long jump · forward
description: A discovered three-cell jump uses one complete body traversal over its longer airtime. Compare jump-long-reverse for the return direction.

title: Long jump · reverse
description: The reverse of the three-cell flat-ground jump. All frames of the same body clip span the full flight and settle into Idle at the native endpoint.

title: Two opportunity attacks → one jump
description: Two actual opportunity subtrees play sequentially at the grounded launch contact. Both complete before one uninterrupted flight; their native event identities, damage and order are retained.

title: Later-step reactor · launch reach limitation
description: The reactor is legally in reach only at the later native Step, beyond melee reach of the visual launch contact. This exposes the current grounded-prefix spatial limitation without moving the reactor or changing native OA eligibility.

title: Demon — Dretch
description: Native creature movement and ordinary attack, followed by a duel with a Fighter. Its own canonical stats, defenses and packaged rig; four cameras share the same history. Dretch uses Demon Beast art; Fetid Cloud/telepathy and multiattack presentation are outside this clip.

title: Melee → remove sword → surviving bow, same turn
description: A Fighter starts with sword and bow and no shield. After melee it publicly unequips the sword; native reconciliation selects the surviving bow before ranged Extra Attack. The saved history must retain that pre-attack stance and the sword's move into inventory.

title: Walk into view → discover current gear and HP → ranged attack
description: Walking discovers an actor that changed sword to dagger and lost HP while unseen. Its first visible state uses the received 33 HP and current dagger, then the observer attacks with its longbow. Earlier private mutations are not replayed as visible actions.

title: Later actor deployment → current appearance → ranged attack
description: A later native deployment reveals a clothed actor absent from the initial scene, after its hidden gear and HP changes. The received admission supplies current identity, equipment and 33 HP before the subsequent longbow attack.

description: Shared faction does not reveal an invisible ally. The subject walks, then voluntarily drops concentration. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; allied factions.

title: True Seeing → invisible opponent
description: The perceiver actually casts True Seeing before the opponent becomes invisible; movement remains perceived and concentration removal restores the original appearance. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; opposing factions.

title: True Seeing → invisible ally
description: The same recorded True Seeing grant and Invisibility sequence with allied factions. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; allied factions.

description: An invisible subject is acquired when the perceiver casts True Seeing. Native turns expire its ten-round effect; playback pauses before the initial Invisibility release while latest has already lost truesight. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; opposing factions.

title: Invisible doorway crossing with truesight
description: Truesight perceives invisibility through the open aperture while the ordinary wall still conceals the rest of the movement. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; opposing factions.

title: Bright Hide → enemy observation blocks
description: Native action discovery does not offer Hide while an enemy sees the subject in bright light. No rejected action, Stealth roll or action cost is fabricated. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; opposing factions.

title: Bright Hide → allied observer
description: An allied observer does not veto the Hide action. Its high Stealth result still changes actual contact because faction does not bypass native concealment. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; allied factions.

title: Dim Hide → successful concealment
description: A native high Stealth roll conceals the subject during movement. A ranged attack reveals the subject through the existing Hidden handler. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; opposing factions.

title: Dim Hide → detected despite Hidden
description: The native low Stealth roll applies Hidden but fails to beat the perceiver; the actor remains visible during movement and attack. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; opposing factions.

title: Hidden + Invisible versus truesight
description: True Seeing bypasses Invisibility but not the high native Stealth DC. Movement stays concealed until a native attack removes both conditions. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; opposing factions.

title: Low Stealth with truesight → casting reveal
description: A low dim-light Hide roll remains detectable to the truesight perceiver. Fire Bolt removes Hidden through its native casting handler. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; opposing factions.

title: True Seeing potion → invisible opponent
description: The perceiver drinks an actual one-charge potion, paying its bonus action and gaining the existing True Seeing effect before the opponent casts Invisibility. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; opposing factions.

title: True Seeing potion → invisible ally
description: The same native potion grant, charge consumption and Invisibility sequence with allied factions. Views: subject (caster/hidden actor) and perceiver; allied factions.
